class.name: NetwSpawnerRoster
class.brief_description: The spawners one session has discovered, and which of them produced each route this peer materialized.
class.description: The engine never announces a [MultiplayerSpawner] as a unit, only its tracked nodes, so this roster is built by the adapter rather than read from anywhere. Both books hold ids and resolve them at each use. A spawner freed mid-session drops out of the roster as it is read, which is why [method live] prunes rather than answering instances that are gone, and a producer that is gone is answered as [code]null[/code] rather than as a freed instance. A route's producing spawner is TAKEN by the despawn that needs it, because the route dies with the node and a second answer would name a spawner for a node nothing holds. [codeblock] roster.enrol(spawner) once per spawner per session roster.live() the ones still alive, pruned roster.note_producer(route, s) this peer built the route through s roster.take_producer(route) the despawn's one answer [/codeblock]

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets every spawner and every producer, which is what a session end means for both books.

method.name: enrol
method.description: Enrols [param spawner] and answers whether it is new to this session. Enrolling [code]null[/code] does nothing and answers [code]false[/code].

method.name: live
method.description: Every enrolled spawner still alive, dropping the ones that are not. The prune happens here because a read is the only moment the roster learns an instance is gone.

method.name: note_producer
method.description: Records that this peer materialized [param route] through [param spawner].

method.name: produced_count
method.description: Routes this peer materialized through [param spawner] and has not despawned, which is the receiver-side half of the spawn limit.

method.name: size
method.description: Spawners enrolled, counted as of the last [method live].

method.name: take_producer
method.description: The spawner that produced [param route], forgetting it in the same act. Answers [code]null[/code] for a route nothing produced and for one whose spawner is gone.
